title: Alpha runway — operator notes and micro-checklist
content:
Purpose: quick personal runbook for alpha release day (small infra changes + model swap). Keep short — this is my pocket checklist and running log. Not the canonical runbook; see Confluence link above for the formal steps.

Timeline (local times):
- 03:30 — wake, coffee, quick Slack scan (#release-ops, #infra-oncall)
- 04:00 — preflight (smoke tests, DB read replica lag check, infra capacity)
- 04:30 — start canary traffic to model-v2 on dedicated pool (10%)
- 05:00 — if canary stable -> ramp to 50%
- 05:30 — full cutover -> monitor 15m, if OK mark done

Quick preflight checks (must run even if someone else did):
- k get pods -n redwood-serving | grep model-v2 -> ensure READY=1/1
- k -n redwood-serving exec deploy/redis -- redis-cli info persistence | grep rdb_bgsave_in_progress
- curl -s https://internal-metrics/api/health | jq .
- check DB replica lag: SELECT pg_last_xact_replay_timestamp(); compare to now()
- confirm canary bucket configured in config-service (rev: config-2026-02-26)

Immediate cutover checklist (tick as you do):
- [ ] Post preflight summary in #release-ops: short list of checks + green/red
- [ ] Lock deploys: set release flag in infra-ops: /release lock alpha-2026-03
- [ ] Kick off canary (10%) — github action: .github/workflows/cutover-alpha.yml -> run
- [ ] Note canary PR/ID in log (PR#4893)
- [ ] Run smoke generator against canary endpoints (10k tokens over 5m)
- [ ] Watch latency SLOs: p50/p95/p99 (dashboard: /d/svc/latency/alpha)
- [ ] If errors > 2% in 5m -> rollback canary (command notes below)
- [ ] On green -> ramp to 50% then 100% (staged every 10m)

Rollback / mitigation quick commands:
- api rollback (canary): curl -XPOST https://ops-api/release/rollback -d '{"tag":"alpha-canary-4893"}'
- scale down model-v2: kubectl scale --replicas=0 deploy/model-v2 -n redwood-serving
- route traffic back to model-v1: /ops route set --service inference --variant model-v1
- if DB concerns -> promote read replica: kubectl apply -f promote-replica.yaml (manual approval required)

Backport notes (things to watch):
- Backport PRs still open: PR#4865 (hotfix: retry on transient kv-cache error) — needs review from SRE
- PR#4879 (quantization flag edge-case) — may affect length>4k flows, test with long prompt set
- If either lands after cutover -> coordinate with ops to queue small patch window (low traffic hours)

Comms (short messages I send):
- Slack preflight (template): "Preflight complete — infra checks green, canary ready, kicking at 04:30 PT. I'll post updates every 15m. Pager: @oncall-sre if anything > P2."
- Canary OK: "Canary (10%) stable for 15m. Ramping to 50%."
- Rollback: "Rolling back to model-v1 due to elevated error rate (see dashboard)."
- Postmortem note: short bullets + link to logs/alerts + initial hypothesis

Escalation contacts (if pager fails -> call):
- Oncall SRE: Marta Lopez (pager) -> +1-555-0143
- Platform eng lead: Devon Park -> +1-555-0198
- PM for alpha: Leah Nguyen -> slack/leah

Monitoring quick list (what I stare at):
- latency dashboard p50/p95/p99 (service: inference-alpha)
- error rate by model variant (split by customer tier)
- token throughput and GPU util (shouldn’t spike > 85% for > 2min)
- redis/kv cache miss rate (if high -> higher cost, possible cache prime needed)
- slow DB queries table (top 10)

Open questions / TODO to follow up after release:
- Should we add a short-circuit fallback to smaller model for low-tier customers? (ask product)
- Signal to add to dashboards for quantization-fallback events
- Confirm if dedicated pool autoscaler threshold is too aggressive (observed 2x thrash in last test)

Personal notes & gotchas (for next time):
- Don’t forget to disable synthetic load generator if you hand off to post-release smoke team
- Keep a short list of customer-facing lines ready for CS (two variants: "minor observability blip" vs "degraded performance, workaround applied")
- When ramping, wait full aggregation window (10m) before next decision — otherwise you chase noise

Run log (use during ops, append lines with timestamp):
- 2026-03-10 03:45 — preflight: all checks green, started canary (10%)
- 2026-03-10 04:00 — smoke tests: p95 +10ms, errors stable 0.3%
- 2026-03-10 04:20 — ramped to 50%; minor DB latency spike at 04:18 (resolved)
- 2026-03-10 04:40 — cutover to 100% complete; monitoring closely

Notes to self: write up a brief postmortem template that highlights quantization regressions and cache-behavior separately. Keep this doc short and portable — drop into my personal notes for quick reference on next run.
